fluff.overview:
The Shootist was introduced in 2621 by Mitchell Vehicles as a command 'Mech for the SLDF's Royal BattleMech regiments stationed within the Terran Hegemony. Originally intended to serve as an electronic warfare-capable battlefield command platform, the seventy-ton design was eclipsed in that role just ten years later by the BattleMaster. The Star League Army reassigned the Shootist to serve as a close-combat juggernaut for heavy lances and as a personal bodyguard for battlefield commanders. The design's balanced mix of firepower, speed, and heavy armor protection proved well suited to both roles.

Production was never prolific, and the devastation of the Succession Wars reduced the Shootist to near extinction. Since that era, the design has been found almost exclusively in ComStar and Word of Blake formations, supplemented by rare examples recovered from Clan Brian Caches.
fluff.capabilities:
The Shootist was designed to prioritize armor protection over raw firepower, a philosophy stemming from the design's original role as a battlefield command platform. The 'Mech carries twelve tons of MV ferro-fibrous armor on a standard frame, and the inclusion of CASE allows the Shootist to survive a catastrophic ammunition explosion that would cripple or destroy most other Star League-era designs.

While firepower was not the primary design consideration, the Shootist carries a formidable arsenal. The Blankenburg extended-range large laser serves as the design's primary long-range weapon, engaging targets at nearly six hundred meters. At closer ranges, the devastating Deathgiver autocannon/20 dominates, capable of crippling light 'Mechs and staggering heavier opponents in a single salvo. Two Blankenburg medium pulse lasers and a Dinatech Mark III small laser round out the arsenal for close-in defense. Pulse technology had only recently been perfected when the Shootist entered production, and its designers took full advantage.

The combination of a standard engine and CASE provides exceptional battlefield survivability, allowing the Shootist to absorb punishment that would disable XL-equipped designs of similar tonnage.
fluff.history:
The Shootist's origins trace to 2621, when Mitchell Vehicles developed the design for the Star League Defense Force's Royal BattleMech regiments stationed within the Terran Hegemony. Initially conceived as an electronic warfare-capable command 'Mech, the design was reassigned to a close-combat juggernaut role after the BattleMaster proved superior in the command niche. The Shootist found its place as a heavy lance anchor and commander's bodyguard, roles that suited its balanced mix of armor, speed, and firepower.

Production of the Shootist was never substantial. Even during the height of Star League manufacturing, output barely kept pace with combat losses. Mitchell Vehicles operated facilities on both New Earth and Terra, but the New Earth plant was destroyed during the Amaris Civil War. The remaining Terra facility fell under ComStar's control in the wake of the Star League's dissolution, and Jerome Blake ordered the production lines mothballed as a precaution against future aggression by the Successor Lords.

Throughout the Succession Wars, the Shootist dwindled toward extinction. Those few surviving examples were jealously hoarded by ComStar, kept in storage facilities against future need. The Com Guards deployed the Shootist almost exclusively with heavy and command Level IIs, where its survivability and firepower anchored defensive formations. Particularly paranoid commanders were known to assign a Shootist as a personal battlefield bodyguard, and the SLDF had long recognized that Shootists worked well together in pairs, though their limited availability prohibited such concentrations.

The brutal fighting on Tukayyid in 3052 took a heavy toll on ComStar's Shootist inventory, and the subsequent schism that formed the Word of Blake further divided the remaining numbers. The Word of Blake reopened the Mitchell Vehicles plant on Terra after securing the world, placing upgraded variants into production by 3062. Despite these efforts, violent clashes between Com Guard and Blakist forces in the Chaos March only accelerated attrition for this classic Star League design.

By the late 3060s, fewer than fifty Shootists remained in the Inner Sphere, and unless the Word of Blake's renewed production could keep pace with losses, experts predicted the current conflict would spell the end for the redoubtable Shootist. The Jihad confirmed those fears, as Coalition forces struck the Mitchell Vehicles plant on Terra with devastating effect. In the post-Jihad era, the Republic of the Sphere assumed control of the facility and eventually resumed limited production, though the Shootist remains one of the rarest BattleMech designs still in service.
fluff.deployment: The original ST-8A configuration has remained unchanged since its 2621 introduction, serving as the standard Shootist fielded throughout the Star League era and the Succession Wars. ComStar hoarded the majority of surviving examples, deploying them almost exclusively with heavy and command Level IIs where their exceptional survivability anchored defensive formations. Following the Word of Blake's reopening of the Mitchell Vehicles plant on Terra, a small number of newly produced ST-8As supplemented the dwindling inventory, though most new-build Shootists received the upgraded ST-8C configuration instead.
